punchline: Planners emptied 36,000 beds for a wave of breakdown that, in the records, mostly did not come.
thirty_sec: Before 1939 Britain expected air raids to cause mass panic and mental illness, and cleared 36,000 beds. After the Blitz began in 1940, records showed few raid-induced breakdowns, yet Mass-Observation reported hysteria in Coventry and the government withdrew its reports. Historians still weigh both stories.
question: What worst-case prediction are you currently acting on, and what real evidence could you collect in the next two weeks to check it?
key_contrast: The forecast said panic; the admission records said mostly not, and one dissenting report was shelved.
